cards.explanation: The answer is the treasuries of God's house. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, takes the silver, the gold and all the furnishings his father David had dedicated, and he places them in the treasuries of the house of God (2 Chronicles 5:1). The temple is done, so the gifts go inside it. Nothing gets left on the porch like a package nobody signed for.

The answer is ark. Solomon gathers the elders to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David (2 Chronicles 5:2). That's the whole reason everybody is being called to Jerusalem, friends. Big gathering, big job.

The answer is False. The text says that when all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites took up the ark (2 Chronicles 5:4). Solomon, Israel's king, is the one who assembled the elders (2 Chronicles 5:2), but the Levites are the ones who take it up.

The answer is counted. Solomon and the whole congregation sacrifice so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered (2 Chronicles 5:6). Nobody could keep a tally, friends. I'd have lost track somewhere around the second ox.

The answer is the Most Holy Place. The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place (2 Chronicles 5:7). It rests beneath the wings of the cherubim there, friends. The ark has a place, and that's it.

The answer is nothing but the two tablets. The text says there was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb (2 Chronicles 5:10). Nothing else was in there, friends, just the two tablets.

The answer is Moses. The text says the two tablets were ones that Moses had placed in the ark at Horeb, where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites after they came out of Egypt (2 Chronicles 5:10). Moses, Israel's leader, is the one who put them in. Same tablets, still there.

The answer is like one voice. The trumpeters and singers joined together to praise and thank the LORD with one voice (2 Chronicles 5:13). Trumpets, cymbals and singers, all praising together, friends.
The answer is a cloud. The singers and trumpeters praise the LORD, and the temple, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud (2 Chronicles 5:13). Stay in your seat for this one, friends.

The answer is True. The cloud fills the house, and the priests could not stand there to minister because of it (2 Chronicles 5:14). They were there to do their work, and the cloud was in the way. I think that's a moment where you just stop what you're doing.

The answer is glory. The priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God (2 Chronicles 5:14). The glory of the LORD is what fills the place, friends. That's the reason the text gives.
